title: Mistaken for Peter Bocage; Amos Riley's parade band
summary: LaCaze says people confused him with Peter Bocage, with whom he worked in street bands, and recalls playing second and third trumpet in Amos Riley's band.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: What's it, it is? 26? I don't remember. No, it's the 27th. Let me, I got it on my watch. It's January 27, 1972. 27. Well, uh, you know, people used to get you mixed up with Bocard. Yeah, the name is Bocard. This is, that's why I just told you about the name, LACAZE and Bocard. A lot of Bocard, uh, they called me, thought I was Peter Bocard. Yeah. Because my name is Peter and his name was Peter. But he's a Bocard and I'm LACAZE. But he know you, because he told me about you. Oh yeah, yeah, I know him well, yeah. I know him well, worked with him quite a bit, you know, in the street bands. Oh yeah. Did you work with many street bands? Well, I never, not too many. But I guess I worked with everyone we had here at one time, you know. I might do one job or two jobs, but I never was a member. I remember one parade band that was Amos Riley. I don't know if you all have worked with him. Yeah, he's still a little bit on the west coast. No, no, that's Amos Riley.
Oh, that's Amos Riley. Amos Riley. Teddy Riley. Teddy Riley's dad.

I guess so. Yeah, look, Teddy was working in Cumberton Street. Yeah, his father, Amos. I worked in his band for quite a while, I mean, second and third trumpet. Did you ever work with the two-lane band? No, no, no, never worked with him. When were you born in Y.A.? Huh? When were you born? 1893. In Henry Orleans? Well, St. Bernard Parish, it's the next parish down here. What town? A plantation or town or a... No, St. Bernard Parish in town, that's the city part.
